name: Cloudstone Curio
oracle_text: Whenever a nonartifact permanent you control enters, you may return another permanent you control that shares a permanent type with it to its owner's hand.
blocked_sentences: Whenever a nonartifact permanent you control enters, you may return another permanent you control that shares a permanent type with it to its owner's hand.

needs.what: a selector clause that matches a candidate whose CARD TYPES intersect the card types of an object bound by the trigger -- the card-type twin of `shares_a_type_with`, e.g. `shares_a_card_type_with: "subject"`, compared on derived `types` (Artifact, Battle, Creature, Enchantment, Land, Planeswalker) rather than on subtypes, so that a creature entering finds the other creatures, a land entering finds the other lands, and an artifact creature entering finds both. Needed on a `return_to_hand` inside a `may` on a `permanent_enters` trigger, alongside `exclude_binding: "subject"` for the printed 'another'
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `shares_a_type_with` is the near miss and is the wrong axis: selectors.py reads `chars(state, other).subtypes` and intersects it with the candidate's subtypes, so it implements '...that shares a CREATURE type with it' (Goblin with Goblin). Written on this card it would return another Goblin when a Goblin entered and would find nothing at all when a typeless permanent or a land entered -- a card that quietly does something narrower than printed. `shares_a_type_with_commander` is subtypes again and points at the commander rather than at the trigger's binding. `types` and `any_types` are literal lists fixed when the card is written, but which permanent type matters is decided at resolution by whatever just entered, so no fixed list expresses the clause; `not_types` (the only other type-side key) has the same problem inverted. There is no condition in `condition_keys` that can read the card types of a binding either, so the line cannot be faked as a `choose_mode` over five type-gated branches -- and that spelling would also hand the choice of type to the wrong place instead of simply letting the controller pick any legal permanent.
